page: Amazon Web Services r5b.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The system is equipped with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. Hardware compute resources consist of 8 physical cores presenting 16 dedicated vCPUs via two threads per core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 128 GB of DDR4 system RAM clocked at 3 GHz, which equates to an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 5 Gbps, with zero integrated GPUs and no bundled local instance storage.

Benchmark results highlight solid throughput across multi-core and memory-heavy operations alongside modest single-core execution speeds. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a multi-core score of 6974.0 and a single-core score of 1133.0, paired with a multi-threaded stress-ng result of 13988.78. Memory bandwidth tests delivered 753.02 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 87.05 GB/sec for large uncached reads, while uncached write bandwidth measured 46.8 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates steady operational capability, registering 13.15 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 5119.53 on the PassMark database operations metric.

The platform presents an efficient balance of capacity for memory-bound tasks without requiring high per-core licensing expenses. The absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage volumes, which should be evaluated against input-output requirements. Consequently, the r5b.4xlarge is well positioned for medium-scale in-memory database management systems, key-value stores such as Redis, enterprise caching tiers, and memory-intensive extract-transform-load jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it incorporates a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor offering 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration is provisioned with 128 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, establishing a generous 8 GB per vCPU allocation designed for memory-intensive applications. It includes a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and contains zero local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent file systems, alongside zero hardware accelerators. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates mid-tier multi-threaded performance, PassMark scores, and Redis processing throughput of 13.15 million operations per second, contrasted by modest single-threaded compute metrics. The r5b.4xlarge delivers balanced resource density for large in-memory caches, relational database systems, and enterprise data processing.
